Short answer: A free Gmail address can work for one person. Google Workspace becomes useful when the business needs email at its domain, organization-owned accounts, shared administration, and controlled offboarding.

What this means for your business

Google’s official comparison distinguishes user-owned accounts from domain-verified organization-owned accounts. The move is about control and administration, not a claim that one email address always lands better.

What to watch

  • Business files and logins tied to a private personal account.
  • A former employee controlling email or recovery.
  • Shared passwords instead of separate managed users.
  • A domain move that accidentally changes email DNS.

Do this next

  1. List the people and shared addresses the business needs.
  2. Confirm the business controls the domain.
  3. Plan users, aliases, groups, migration, recovery, and offboarding.
  4. Change DNS in a documented window and test send, receive, calendar, and recovery.

When Little Fight fits

We can set up the domain, accounts, migration, website, forms, and handoff as one plan. The business remains the administrator.
